title: AI integration: The role of AI in Filipino MSMEs and BPO sectors
summary: MANILA, Philippines – Experts believe that greater knowledge on the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) in businesses is essential in promoting and ensuring growth for PH businesses,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Experts believe that greater knowledge on the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI) in businesses is essential in promoting and ensuring growth for PH businesses, especially MSMEs (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises).
During the AIVF Manila 2026 on October 28, Chairman Wilson Chua revealed that he sees the forum as a potential game-changer for the MSME and BPO sector here in the Philippines.

“I think the challenge right now is most of the small or medium companies right now, they’re not ready for AI because AI for them is still too difficult or expensive. They don’t know where to start, they don’t know how to apply AI to their company. So, here, we have many AI agent companies here (that) can help any SME company, and any business can start to use AI,” Chua said.
For them, the country’s international outsourcing industry and demand for AI brought upon by progressive digital transformation make Manila a prime choice for holding the forum.
He also believes that 60% to 70% of the businesses are yet to fully learn about using AI, which is why it is also crucial to accept it as a growing norm in today’s lifestyle.

“AI is not to address the human but to help the human to do their work more efficiently,’ he added.They see AI not just as an option or alternative for making life easy, but a necessity for businesses to grow with the breakthroughs in technology.

Organized by the AI Vision Global Alliance Limited and Hong Kong Polytechnic University Hangzhou Technology and Innovation Research Institute, the AI Vision Forum Manila assures that there is a potential for AI to achieve a service that is more inclusive for businesses.

Attendees were able to learn more about how artificial intelligence can ease some parts of business operations through representatives from builder AI platforms such as HowOne and Duck Reels and assistance providers like Soric, S.H.I.E.L.D., A3SEO, and TRXY.

Cloud partners from TrueWatch, Oracle, TiDB, Alibaba, and Cloudflare also held a panel discussion to provide answers to some of the infrastructure-related questions that may help businesses and decision-makers know better what they should work on. Enterprises and decision-makers also had the chance to build their network during the event.
Following Manila, the organizers intend to bring the AI Vision Forum to Barcelona and Hong Kong for its next stops.
